title: Weak population structure in Arctic cod (Boreogadus saida) across its circumpolar range as determined from a meta-analysis
content:
Abstract
Arctic cod (Boreogadus saida) is a key forage fish that plays a central role in Arctic marine food webs. Despite its ecological importance and circumpolar distribution, the extent and drivers of its population structure across the Arctic Ocean remain unclear. Here, we conducted a meta-analysis of published genetic studies on Arctic cod, combining FST estimates across the species’ range to assess consensus patterns of population differentiation and examine ecological and methodological sources of variation among studies. Across its circumpolar range, genetic differentiation (FST) appears consistently low but significantly different from zero, indicating weak yet detectable population structure. At the broad scale, differentiation is higher among regions than within regions and shows weak isolation by distance. At finer spatial scales, we found no evidence of consistent genetic differentiation between nearshore and offshore habitats. However, substantial heterogeneity in FST estimates remains unexplained, suggesting that variation in population structure may reflect processes operating at finer spatial or genomic scales than those captured by existing studies. Future work integrating genomic architecture with ecological data across circumpolar scales will be necessary to better understand the mechanisms shaping Arctic cod population structure.
